question.text: Will at least 450 MEPs vote in favour of the European Parliament's resolution on further EU sanctions against Russia on 12 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least 450 Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) vote in favour of Parliament's resolution on further EU sanctions against Russia at the plenary vote on 12 November 2026. The relevant figure is the number of votes in favour recorded for the final vote on the text put to Parliament as its resolution on "Further EU sanctions against Russia in response to the escalating attacks against Ukraine: cutting of the sources financing the Russian war" (procedure 2026/2949(RSP)) at the sitting of 12 November 2026; where several motions for resolutions (B10 documents) are tabled, this means the vote on the joint motion, or whichever motion is voted as the resolution as a whole. The figure is the official tally as first published in Parliament's "Minutes – Results of votes" for that sitting, linked from https://www.europarl.europa.eu/plenary/en/votes.html and from the adopted-text listing at https://www.europarl.europa.eu/plenary/en/texts-adopted.html, and votes on individual amendments do not count. If the resolution is rejected, or if no vote on such a resolution is held on 12 November 2026 (for example because no resolution is tabled or the vote is postponed to a later sitting), the question resolves No.
question.fine_print: A vote taken on any date other than 12 November 2026 does not count, including a vote on the other day of the same part-session (11 November 2026). Later notices correcting how individual MEPs voted do not change the tally used for resolution.

research:
I couldn't confirm that a resolution vote on this item will happen on 12 November. Agenda listings show the debate, and one site lists the item among expected Thursday votes. But Parliament's own pages either didn't load or didn't confirm a vote. Recent comparable resolutions passed with 432 to 482 votes in favour, so 450 sits in the middle of that range.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-02: The official agenda PDF (the SYN_PDOJ link in the background) and the agenda page for 12 November returned no content when fetched. The official votes and texts-adopted pages for 12 November can't show results until the sitting takes place. [EP agenda PDF](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/sedcms/documents/PRIORITY_INFO/1820/SYN_PDOJ_November%20I_BRU_EN.pdf)
- 2026-11-02: The Legislative Observatory page for 2026/2949(RSP) says "Awaiting plenary debate/vote", procedure type Rule 136(2), resolution on a statement. It lists no events, and its only date is an **indicative plenary date of 11/11/2026**, not 12/11. Nothing on the page confirms a vote is scheduled. [OEIL](https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/procedure-file?reference=2026/2949(RSP))
- EP Votes, a third-party tracker, lists the debate at 09:00 on Thu 12 Nov, and a separate EP Votes page reportedly lists the item among expected Thursday votes. I couldn't open these pages myself (403 error), so I'm relying on the search summary. [epvotes](https://epvotes.com/week/2026-W46)
- I found no B10 motion for a resolution or joint motion for this item yet.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. The plenary is on 11 and 12 November in Brussels.
- One open uncertainty: the 11 vs 12 November date mismatch. Resolutions on statements are sometimes voted at a later part-session, which would resolve the question No.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-10-30 to 11-02: 21 MEPs from several groups wrote to von der Leyen and the IIHF, the ice hockey federation, calling for new sanctions and visa restrictions after a Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling let Russian hockey teams return to international competition. This shows backing for sanctions across groups, but it is not a plenary act. [Yle](https://yle.fi/a/7-10107925), [UNN](https://unn.ua/en/news/21-mep-calls-for-new-sanctions-against-russia-over-the-return-of-its-national-hockey-teams-to-international-tournaments)
- 2026-10-22: The Black Sea resolution (calling for an EU naval operation) passed 432 to 52, with 88 abstentions. [Pravda.ua](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/23/8059350/), [IEU Monitoring](https://ieu-monitoring.com/editorial/eu-parliament-calls-for-naval-operation-in-black-sea-after-russian-attacks/1252949/)
- 2026-10-12: The Council agreed its largest-ever round of listings, 826 companies and 743 individuals. [Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/10/12/russia-s-war-of-aggression-against-ukraine-eu-agrees-largest-ever-package-of-listings-targeting-almost-1600-individuals-and-entities-in-russia-s-military-industrial-complex/)
- 2026-10-08: The Duma elections resolution passed 482 to 41, with 39 abstentions. It calls for further sanctions. [Brussels Times](https://www.brusselstimes.com/2352443/meps-reject-russian-elections-condemn-fear-driven-ballot-and-occupied-region-votes)
- 2026-07-23: The EU adopted its 21st sanctions package. [Commission](https://finance.ec.europa.eu/news/eu-adopts-21st-package-sanctions-against-russia-2026-07-23_en)

## 4. Base rates
Votes in favour on 2026 resolutions related to Russia and Ukraine:
- 2026-02-24: Four years of war, 437 / 82 / 70 (for / against / abstentions). [Lovguiden](https://lovguiden.dk/en/det-offentlige/europa-parlamentet/2026-04-30-europa-parlamentet-kraever-retfaerdighed-og-erstatning-til-civile-ofre-i-ukraine)
- 2026-04-30: Accountability for attacks on civilians, 446 / 63 / 52. This is the vote the background describes as approving the 20th package. It is a broader resolution that welcomed the package, not a vote on the package itself. A claims commission text that day got 465 votes in favour. [Euromaidan Press](https://euromaidanpress.com/2026/04/30/european-parliament-backs-establishment-of-a-special-tribunal-for-russia/)
- 2026-10-08: Duma elections, 482 votes in favour. The background reports other motions that day at 381 to 541; I did not verify those.
- 2026-10-22: Black Sea, 432 votes in favour.
- Of the main resolutions above, only 1 of 4 reached 450 (482). Counting the claims commission vote, it's 2 of 5. The figures range from about 430 to 480, with a midpoint around 445.
- Brussels mini-sessions and Thursday votes often have lower turnout than Strasbourg weeks. This is a general pattern; I have no specific figures for it.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this vote.
- Loosely related markets (2026-11-02): Polymarket puts "EU lifts ban on Russian diesel imports by Dec 31" at 4.4% and "EU country blames Russia for new sabotage attack by Nov 30" at 53.5%. Kalshi puts "Graham Act sanctions take effect before 2027" at 15%. None of these bears directly on the vote count.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- When motions are tabled: whether there is a joint motion and which groups sign it, especially ECR and The Left.
- The final agenda adopted at the opening of the sitting on 11 November, which could move the vote or carry it over to a later part-session.
- Possible progress on the 22nd package or new Russian attacks before 12 November, which could raise support.
- Turnout on Thursday 12 November, voting session 11:00 to 13:00 CET.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The outcome will be known by about 12 November 2026, roughly 10 days away. For Yes, two things must happen. First, a resolution on procedure 2026/2949(RSP) must actually be put to a final vote at the 12 November sitting, not on 11 November and not carried over to a later session. Second, that final vote must record at least 450 votes in favour in the official "Results of votes" minutes.

(b) Status quo: no motion for a resolution has been tabled yet and no deadline for motions has been published. If nothing changes, there is no vote, which resolves No. If the vote goes ahead and support stays at recent levels, the tally would land around 430 to 450, just under the threshold.

(c) Base rate: in 2026, comparable Russia/Ukraine resolutions recorded 437, 446, 465, 482 and 432 votes in favour. That is 2 of 5 at or above 450, about 40%, assuming a vote takes place. Brussels mini-sessions and Thursday votes tend to have somewhat lower turnout, which pulls this down slightly.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The 8 October Duma resolution reached 482.
  - The topic is sanctions, which has broad support across groups.
  - The Council's record listings on 12 October and the escalating attacks may lift support.
  - The agenda places the vote at 11:00 on 12 November, right after the debate.
- **For No:**
  - The most recent comparable vote, the 22 October Black Sea resolution, got only 432.
  - The resolution that welcomed the 20th package got 446.
  - The Legislative Observatory gives an indicative date of 11 November and lists no events.
  - No B10 motions had been tabled as of 2 November.
  - A mini-session Thursday usually means lower attendance.
  - The group arithmetic is tight. EPP, S&D, Renew and Greens hold about 454 seats in total, and with ordinary absences they fall well short of 450 without substantial ECR and Left votes.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The vote happens with about 560 votes cast. ECR mostly abstains, Patriots and ESN vote against, and the resolution passes with around 435 in favour. Alternatively, the vote slips to the late-November Strasbourg session.
- **Yes:** A broad joint motion signed by EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens and ECR, with high Thursday attendance after a fresh Russian attack, draws around 470 in favour.

(f) Moving to a final number: I put the chance that a final vote is actually held on 12 November at about 70%, because of the date mismatch, the missing motion deadline and the risk of a carry-over. Conditional on a vote, I put the chance of reaching 450 at about 37%, a little below the 40% base rate because of mini-session turnout and the lower recent results. Combined, 0.70 × 0.37 is about 26%. There is no market covering this exact question.

Probability: 26%

(a) The outcome will be known on 12 November 2026, about 10 days from now, with the official tally published the same day. For Yes, Parliament must hold the final vote on the 2026/2949(RSP) resolution (the joint motion, or whichever text is voted as a whole) on 12 November, and at least 450 MEPs must vote in favour.

(b) If nothing changed, a vote would most likely take place on 12 November and the motion would pass with roughly 430 to 470 votes in favour. Without a confirmed vote and a vote count, the status quo outcome is No.

(c) Base rate: in 2026, comparable Russia/Ukraine resolutions passed with 437, 446, 465 (claims commission), 482 and 432 votes in favour. That is 2 of 5 at or above 450, about 40%. Same-day votes on 8 October ranged from 381 to 541. The vote also has to actually happen on 12 November. Resolutions on statements are sometimes carried over, and OEIL lists 11 November as the indicative date, which adds risk. I put the chance of a vote on 12 November at about 75-80%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The topic is sanctions, which the EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens and most of the ECR support.
  - The Duma resolution on 8 October drew 482 votes in favour.
  - Escalating Russian attacks, including on Black Sea shipping, and the record listings agreed on 12 October could build a broad coalition.
  - The agenda places a voting session immediately after the debate.
- **For No:**
  - Brussels mini-session Thursday votes tend to have low turnout. Total votes cast have been around 560-575, so 450 needs about 79% of votes cast in favour.
  - The most recent comparable vote, Black Sea on 22 October, got only 432 in favour, with 88 abstentions.
  - The vote on the 20th sanctions package resolution got 446.
  - Energy and oil-revenue provisions may push parts of The Left and the ECR to abstain.
  - No motion-for-resolution deadline has been published yet, and the date shows a mismatch between 11 and 12 November.

(e) No scenario: the joint motion is tabled without full ECR backing, and Thursday attendance is thin. It passes 438 to 60, with 70 abstentions. Alternatively, the vote is moved to the November II session.
Yes scenario: a fresh Russian strike on EU territory before the vote rallies the groups. EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens and ECR co-sign the joint motion, and it passes 471 to 55, with 40 abstentions.

(f) I start from about 40% conditional on a vote taking place, roughly the base rate. I shade that slightly down to about 38% for the Brussels Thursday turnout and the energy-sanctions content, then multiply by a roughly 78% chance that the vote happens on 12 November. That gives about 30%.

Probability: 30%

**(a) Time left and what has to happen for Yes.** About 10 days remain; the outcome will be known on 12 November 2026. For Yes, three things must all happen:
- A resolution on procedure 2026/2949(RSP) is tabled.
- It is voted in the 12 November voting session, not on 11 November and not carried over to a later part-session.
- At least 450 MEPs vote in favour on the final vote, per the official "Results of votes" minutes.

**(b) Status quo outcome.** The debate is scheduled, but no motion for a resolution has been found yet. The Legislative Observatory lists an indicative date of 11 November, which conflicts with the 12 November debate slot. Recent comparable tallies sit just below 450. If nothing changes, the most likely outcome is No, either because support falls short of 450 or because the vote is held on another date.

**(c) Base rate.** Among recent 2026 Russia/Ukraine resolutions, the main votes reached 450 about 1 in 4 times (2 in 5 counting the claims commission vote). The tallies were 437, 446, 482 and 432, plus 465.
- Brussels mini-sessions and Thursday votes tend to have lower turnout, which pushes the tally down.
- Thursday debates on statements in mini-sessions are often, but not always, voted the same day. I put the chance of a vote actually happening on 12 November at about 70-75%.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - The 8 October Duma elections resolution passed with 482 votes in favour.
  - Sanctions against Russia attract broad support: EPP, S&D, Renew and the Greens, plus most of ECR (PiS, Fratelli d'Italia, Baltic members) and part of The Left.
  - Escalating Russian attacks and the work on a 22nd package could encourage a broad joint motion.
- **For No:**
  - The 22 October Black Sea resolution reached only 432.
  - The 30 April resolution reached 446.
  - The 24 February resolution reached 437.
  - On 2 November, the Legislative Observatory showed an indicative date of 11 November and no motion for a resolution had been found, so the timing is uncertain.
  - Thursday turnout in a Brussels mini-session is likely lower than in Strasbourg weeks.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** A joint motion passes on Thursday with about 440 in favour, 60 against and 50 abstentions, because attendance is thin and Left and ECR members split. Alternatively, the vote is moved to the late-November Strasbourg session.
- **Yes:** A joint motion is signed by EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens and ECR. Attendance is high, and it passes with about 470 in favour.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** Given that a vote happens, I put the chance of at least 450 in favour at about 40%. That is slightly above the raw base rate, because a sanctions-focused text draws ECR support, but held down by mini-session turnout. Multiplying by the roughly 72% chance that the vote is held on 12 November gives about 29%.

Probability: 29%

(b) Status quo: no vote has been held yet. Neither the agenda placement nor the size of the joint motion is settled. Recent sanctions-focused tallies have landed just below 450, so if nothing changes the default leans No.

(c) Base rate: recent Russia/Ukraine final-vote tallies in this term were 412, 432, 437, 446, 465 and 482. That is 2 of 6 at 450 or more, about 33%. (d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - On 8 October the Duma resolution got 482 votes.
  - Escalation is ongoing: Black Sea strikes and drone incursions.
  - The 22nd package is in preparation and is possibly due in November, which could help a broad joint motion that includes ECR.

- **For No:**
  - On 22 October the Black Sea resolution got only 432 votes.
  - On 30 April the 20th-package resolution got 446.
  - It is a Brussels mini-session, and the vote is on the last day, when attendance is usually lower.
  - The OEIL indicative date is 11 November, and no B10 motions had been tabled as of 2 November.
  - The vote could be carried over to a later sitting.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The vote happens on Thursday, but ECR splits and attendance is thin. The tally comes in at about 435-445, similar to the April and October sanctions texts. Alternatively, the vote is moved to the December Strasbourg session.
- **Yes:** EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens and ECR co-sign a joint motion after another major Russian strike. Turnout is about 575, and the text gets 455-480 in favour, as the Duma resolution did.

(f) I start from a conditional chance of about 33% that the tally clears 450 if the vote is held. Specific escalation and the pending 22nd package lift this slightly, to about 35%, while mini-session, last-day attendance pulls it back down. I then multiply by about 0.75-0.8 for the chance that a qualifying vote actually takes place on 12 November. That gives roughly 26-28%, and I settle at about 27%.

Probability: 27%
